Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "A student possesses a plot of land, bounded by the four great continents.
Now that it has been brought before the blind hall, how shall it be managed? The Master said: "I wish for you, Venerable One, from this day forward..."

"Day by day it is no better than the day before. Jin said, "It would be such that the Buddhas of the three periods, the six generations of patriarchs, and the monks throughout the world would not dare to look upon you with a direct eye.
The Master said, "Have you yet broken up your household and scattered your home? Jin said, "Where are the eyes of the ancestral teacher?
The Master said, "Since the four boundaries are already distinct, where does the seal of verification lie?"

[The monk] stood before him. The monk continued, "My heart does not betray others, and my face shows no color of shame. The Master said, "You conceited fellow! You have deceived the official authorities;
you shall undergo severe punishment! The monk prostrated himself. Thereupon [the Master] cited the case of Hanshan asking Master Fenggan:
"If an ancient mirror has not been polished, how can it reflect? Fenggan said, "A crystal pitcher contains no images; a monkey reaches for the moon in the water. Hanshan said, "This is still..."
"It does not illuminate. "Please, Master, speak further. Gan said, "The myriad virtues have not been brought forth;
how am I to speak? The Master said, "Great Hanshan! You have shamelessly deceived Fenggan right in his face.
Great Fenggan, upon being questioned by Hanshan, it turns out you were small-hearted. Now tell me, where was he small-hearted? Where was there deception?"
“Mán! Three days ago, this mountain monk saw what looked like an excellent game of fresh-faced chess.
It is a pity it was ruined by those two old, frozen leeches. Is there now any monk who can move along a living path?”
"Even if you come forward first, watch the very first move. He clapped his hands and said, "Finished. He then ascended the hall and said:

"On this fine night of the fifteenth day of the third month, the songs of the gods and the dances of the ghosts continue as before; there is no need for three or four more bouts of spitting and swallowing."
Behold the swallowing and spitting out of seven or eight; Linji’s blind donkey rides backward. Yunmen’s True Dharma Eye is universal;
these three men have certified the turtle as a tortoise. Let the patch-robed monks puff with their breath as they will—do not puff! The sweet is sweet, and the bitter is bitter.
The crescent moon and the long snake need not be displayed; when the trigger is pulled, there is naturally the thousand-jin crossbow. [He] struck the meditation seat and descended from it.
On the first day of the month, he ascended the hall and cited Master Deshan. One day, because Attendant Kuok asked, "Where have all the sages of the past gone?
Deshan said, "What? What? The Master said, "The rice is finished, down to the husks. Kuok said, "An Imperial Edict."
"Setting the flying dragon horse free, the lame tortoise pokes its head out. Shanhui departs. The Master says, "One does not avoid taboo words when composing a literary work.
The next day, after bathing, Guo comes to serve tea to Shanhui. Shanhui pats Guo’s back once and asks, "Regarding yesterday’s *kōan*, what was it?
The Master says, "From beginning to end, it was but a grandmotherly heart. Guo says, "This old fellow has only just now woken up. The Master [laughs].

He said, "Using a winter melon seal upside down. He further said, "How could one tie a knot on a bowstring? [The other] asked, "What harm is there in tying a knot? [He replied,] "One cannot pave flowers upon a stone surface.
[The other] asked, "What harm is there in paving flowers? "This old fellow Deshan," he continued, "ordinarily drives away spirits with his white staff and grasps wind and clouds with bare hands;
yet it turns out his sleeves are too short for his arms and his shoes are too wide for his thin feet. Now, let us put him to the test."
The questioner knows only where it goes; he does not know where it comes from. The respondent knows only where it comes from; he does not know where it goes.
In one question and one answer, there is always something at stake. Just as when Deshan said, "Rest," how will you all deliberate upon this?
[He] strikes the meditation staff and says: "The 'Yangchun' and 'Baixue' have no one to sing along with; the 'Liushui' and 'Gao-shan' require careful examination."

"Look! Entering the hall, this mountain monk has a fault: it exhausts the very core of the patch-robed monks, startles the iron ox of Shanzhou, and swallows up the mountains, rivers, and the great earth.
He strikes the meditation staff once and says, "This is the staff of Xiatang; is it not?"
It is accomplished. One may call it a staff, or one may not call it a staff; it is not that it is not, nor is it even "not-not. But tell me: what is it?
It is all achieved through warfare, yet finally dispelled by song and dance. Rest!
Ascending the hall: In the fourth month, as summer gradually approaches and the heat increases, one must practice skillful healing through proper self-regulation.

Manjusri pulls the tendons from within the eyes; Vajra extracts the wedge from behind the head. Sumeru leaps up into the sky; Kunlun from the bottom of the sea sticks out his tongue. How many times has there been long song, and how many times sorrow?
Every time one drinks water, one chokes. Therefore it is said: "When entering a territory, inquire about its customs. My Lord—
If you can understand it upon meeting [the master], you may go straight to the gate and topple the flagpole. If you still do not understand, then you will be exposed as a fraud by Mahākāśyapa.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised up the case where Master Hua-yao Ying addressed the assembly, saying: "Seventeen, eighteen—if you speak of it, you are blind.
Nineteen, twenty—people cannot believe it. Furthermore, one would have to wait for withered wood to sprout flowers, or seek juice from a sesame cake. The Master said:
Xu Liu carries a single board; I am not like that. On the third and the eleventh, there is no need to choose a day.
When the nostrils are pierced through and the eyes protrude, one bumps into a pillar and the task of study is complete.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Xuedou’s instruction to the assembly: “The ten directions have no walls, and the four sides have no gates.
Where did the ancients see their guests? He continued, “If you can utter a phrase that takes up the hand [of the teaching], I grant you dominion over all under heaven.
“Great Assembly, if a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely face immediate anxieties. How could this compare to Guoqing, where the five peaks encircle us on all sides?”
"Surrounded by lotuses at the confluence of two streams, he wanders the mountains when idle and drinks water when thirsty; where is there that is not a place for receiving guests?

He further said, "If you can utter a 'linking phrase,' I will grant you dominion over all under heaven. The Master said, "Ho! Ho! As for the Buddha-dharma and the Way of Chan, there is indeed no lack of a linking phrase;
it would simply be like a great axe striking down through the three gates. After a long silence, he struck with his staff.
He drew a line and asked, "Do you understand? Gejin Ling has hills and valleys within his breast; Chicheng Shan possesses the judgment of spring and autumn within its skin;
Huading Peak has its crown touching the ground; and Tongbai Guan bows its head in prostration. He gave a shout and descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the example of Gold Peak (Jin-feng) Worthy. One day, seeing Linji approaching, he held his staff crosswise.
Linji clapped his hands three times and then went to the meditation hall. After Gold Peak had finished his formal greetings, he asked, "When host and guest meet, each has their own proper etiquette.
Why have you, Venerable Sir, been so discourteous? Linji struck him with his sitting mat. As Gold Peak was about to ask further, Linji struck him again.
"One sitting mat. Feng said, "The mountain monk has lost his advantage," and he immediately returned to the abbot’s quarters.
The Master said, "One person takes a common staff and stirs up the waters of the four great oceans; another uses the uncarved seal to stamp through the void of the ten directions.
Now, you must not move them. To move them is to receive one blow of the staff for your inquiry."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: When Zhaozhou was traveling and arrived at Linji, he was behind the washstand washing his feet. Seeing him, Linji asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou said, "It happens to be the time when the old monk is washing his feet. Linji stepped forward and made a gesture as if listening.

Zhaozhou said, "If you had understood right then, why would you have to peck like a bird? Linji then returned to his quarters. Zhaozhou said: [The Master] said: "This is the 'pecking' that is not yet the 'pecking. This is the 'not pecking' that is not yet the 'not pecking. If you can see through this, you will know that the Patriarch’s coming from the West is not something to be grasped by the intellect; it is a matter of directly pointing to the human heart and seeing one's nature. It is not a matter of seeking outside or following after words and phrases. If you can let go of all such conceptualizations, you will see that the Patriarch’s coming from the West is nothing other than this very moment. Do not seek it elsewhere; do not try to grasp it. It is right here, right now. If you can realize this, you will be free from the delusions of birth and death. If you cannot, you will continue to wander in the cycle of samsara. Therefore, I urge you all: do not waste this precious human life. Exert yourselves with all your might!"
"I have been traveling on foot for thirty years. Today, I have mistakenly provided annotations for others. The Master asked, "Where did Zhaozhou mistakenly provide annotations for others?
After a long silence, he said, "Poverty at home is still tolerable; poverty on the road is what kills one with grief."
Ascending the hall: "Beyond the clouds, a thousand peaks are magnificent; before one's eyes, two streams are clear. If you understand it in such a way, you will suffer in samsara for eons.
Ascending the hall: Master Langya Huijue once ascended the hall. A monk came forward and drew a perfect circle. Langya...
Yunmen struck him, saying, "Speak! Speak! The monk said, "I will not speak; I will not speak. Yunmen struck him again, saying, "Speak! Speak! The monk said, "I will not speak; I will not speak.
Yunmen struck him yet again, saying, "Speak! Speak! The monk said, "The Buddhas of the three periods do not depart from this. Yunmen struck him once more.
He then called for the *karmadāna* (steward) and had the monk expelled from the monastery. Yunmen then ascended the seat and pointed his finger at the monk, saying to the assembly, "Bhikṣu!"
"He commits a *pāyattika* offense; the mountain monk enters hell. The Master picked up the case and said: "If human sentiments were good, even drinking water would make one fat.
Why is it that when a bhikṣu commits a *pāyattika*, Langya instead enters hell? After a long silence, he said: "If you understand, then go and understand.
I, the mountain monk, shall bear witness with you. He then joined his palms and said: "Both giver and receiver shall equally attain the Five Constants."
"May you obtain physical strength, longevity, peace, and unimpeded eloquence.
[The Master] ascends the hall and says: "A monk asked Yunmen, 'What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya? Yunmen said, 'Hide your body within the Big Dipper.
Does anyone here still manage to penetrate it? Master Fu Daoshi said: 'Empty-handed, holding a hoe; walking..."* *(Note: The source text appears to be truncated at this point.)*
One is riding a water buffalo while people pass over a bridge. The bridge flows, yet the water does not flow.
If you call this the Dharma-body, you will enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow; if you do not call this the Dharma-body, you will enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow.
How will you penetrate this? Investigate!
Ascending the hall: This morning is the first day of the seventh month; the annual cycle of the monastic community is drawing to a close.
I now request you to untie your bags and wander freely wherever you may go. Whether you untie them or not, it is all well; if you wish to rest now, then rest.
In the fundamental nature of ordinary beings and sages there is no taboo; Buddhas and demons are both merely enemies. In profound stillness, there is no interference; in bustling clamor, do not...
It can be gathered up. Traveling east, one does not see the benefit of traveling west. When a single leaf falls, one knows the autumn of the world.

On the anniversary of National Teacher Yuanwu’s death, he ascended the hall and said: "The great waves of the Jin River connect with the Three Gorges; the high peaks of Jiu Long join the Five Heavens.
Within them stands a Guide whose mouth grows horns, whose eyebrows have fallen away, and whose heels are pierced through. He strikes the statue of the Lord of Jiazhou..."
The stone Buddha emits fire from his eyes, startling the iron ox of Shanfu. Smoke rises from his nostrils—aha ha! Do not resent Heaven.
Whether there is profit or loss, one does not leave the marketplace. Extending the hand and withdrawing the hand;
no factionalism, no partiality. (He plants his staff and says: "Three or five bowls of strong tea—the intent lies beside the hoe."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the precedent set by Master Daowu, who cited an ancient saying: "To recognize it is as before, yet it is not so. This, too, is difficult to comprehend.
"The rustic dweller has much beard and mustache beneath his chin; the Persian has deep-set eyes and large nostrils. How extraordinary!
In a flash, he passes through the borders of Silla. The Master drew a line with his staff and said, "I only wish for the winds and rains to be harmonious..."

[Seal] State Prosperity. A letter from Chan Master Dahui has arrived. He ascends the hall and says: "The road to Yong is as distant as heaven; when sentiment is forgotten, the Way and its righteousness are deep.
Space has no front or back—where can one seek the sound of home? Is there any monk who knows where my elder brother has gone?"
"Ma! Come out and point it out! A monk asked: "Chan Master Huai’s verse on his passing says:
'The sun rises and shines upon Fusang; floating clouds obscure Mount Hua. At the third watch, he passes through the Iron Ring Mountains, snapping off the horns of the Black Dragon.
Miaoxi said: 'To live is just like this; to die is just like this. Whether there is a verse or no verse—what a fuss! These two venerable masters..."

[The student] asked, "Is there still superiority and inferiority? The Master said, "An iron hammer in the eye of a needle. The student advanced and said, "Transcending the thousand sages, it stands out before the myriad functions.

The Master said, "Idle talk. The student said, "I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: *Note: This dialogue is a classic example from the *Wumenguan* (Gateless Barrier) illustrating the non-dual nature of reality and the inadequacy of conceptualization.*
"I will give you one coin tomorrow. The monk prostrated and said: "The Way is vast, yet no merit is established; there are no corners, and thus no directions exist.
Treading upon the giant tortoise, he chants his hymn and returns to the great ocean; grasping the moon's horn, he emerges from the celestial gate.
This was my Dharma brother, Chan Master Dahui of Jing Mountain. He did not at all consider the gravity of our fraternal bond, nor the purity of our kinship as brothers.
"Deeply grieved! The news of his passing has arrived so suddenly; he has abandoned us and departed. Alas! The True Dharma is fading away and the elders are withering.
We drift upon the sea of suffering as the compassionate boat capsizes. What misfortune for the Gate of the Dharma—what pain could be greater than this? He then suddenly grasped his staff and said:
The great earth is shaken by the Vairambha winds; the Bodhi tree of humans and devas is toppled. White clouds retreat into the vast abyss; a pall of gloom gathers into a mass.

Across the boundless expanse of river and sky, voices cry out, yet none can be brought back. After a long while, he calls out, "Singing Apes! After a long while, he calls again, "Singing Apes! Then he asks, "What is this?
He strikes his meditation seat once and says, "Zhiguang shall not remain in the night. Following this, [he passed away].
While acting as clouds and thunder, he ascended the hall.
Quoting Ciming, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Daowu beats the drum; the four great continents participate together.
When the staff is held horizontally, it encompasses the heavens and the earth; when the alms bowl is turned, it covers the worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. You all..."
"Everyone, where do you establish yourselves and sustain your lives? If you know the place where one establishes oneself and sustains one's life, then even in Uttarakuru one eats gruel and rice.
If you do not know it, then on these long benches one eats gruel and rice. The Master said:
"Making money from lending at interest and selling rice while hoarding the husks—what joy is there in such things? As he spoke, he reached out his hand and then let it drop, saying:
"Thirty years ago, this mountain monk lived in Western Sichuan; thirty years later, I dwell in Eastern Zhejiang.
I do not grasp at grass that lies across me, nor do I tread upon grass that stands upright. Now, however, I am being dragged down by my neighbors. He did not finish speaking.
Having completed the actual offering, he departed. He further remarked: "On the long, continuous beds, they eat porridge and rice as if in Uttarakuru;
yet throughout the entire world, there are enemies.
Upon ascending the hall, he cited Master Baoning Yong’s instruction to the assembly: "One is one, two is two, three is three."
"Four is four; the number is very clear. Above and below, they rely on their respective positions. [The Master asks: "What is the matter with relying on their respective positions?
He then draws a line with his staff and says, "O Assembly! At once, you have thrown the sixty *jiāzhì* cycles into total disorder! The Master said:
Thus, great wealth comes from Heaven; minor wealth comes from Man. One kills a pauper and becomes a wealthy man.
I, this mountain monk, also have a path of the Dharma to present to the assembly. "One is two. Since it is one, why is it actually two?
If you can understand this, your studies are complete. He spoke again: "One is two, two is three. Bite down on your teeth!"
Guan thoroughly investigated this. Amidst the clamor and bustle, he threw it with both hands; in the state of nakedness, he carried it on his two shoulders.

Old Mañjuśrī stubbornly pointed southward, yet the three blows at the gate were truly difficult to swallow. He performed somersaults beneath the Five Peaks and acted like a fool at the crossroads of the eightfold path.
(He lets out a shout. He descends from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff, drew a line, and said: "The great earth and its mountains and rivers do not appear;
empty space breaks into a cold sweat across the entire body. At the tip of the staff, all paths are cut off. Who is it that pulls the sinews from within the eyes of a skull?
Is there anyone here who serves as a local official, a patrol officer, a magistrate, a headman, or a rank-and-file soldier? After a long silence, he called out in a loud voice:
With a single "Nyo! he said: "At the first watch, there is nothing more to do; at the second watch, I entrust the matter to you.
Raise your whole body! Head Seat, stand up as a monk! Entering the tiger’s den and the demon’s palace with wide strides, the plowshare that plows out tongues awaits your arrival.
The nostrils of the one who rubs the clouds, his beard and mustache—when meeting amidst the clamor, the ghosts tear them apart. Not for a moment leaving the mountain of blades."
Dwelling within a horse’s belly, one immediately follows the glowing coals into a donkey’s womb. There is no need to guess at this single phrase;
how could the reception of guests depend on prior arrangement? Beating one’s chest with one hand, where has one gone? A toad wearing green moss upon its head.
Ascending the hall: This morning is the fifth day of the sixth month. To the clear-eyed monk, it is difficult to behold.
Startling the tortoise from its seat, he bites the stone tiger on the street. Grinding the gong, beating the iron drum, he half-heals the idle Buddhas and patriarchs with a broken mouth.
Rising and sitting follow one another as he walks alone; the night watch has deepened, yet the sun stands at noon.

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "When the dripping water freezes and the jade is pure and the ice is clear, what then? The Master said, "If you know the time, it is appropriate; you are fit to be a *śrāmaṇera*.
The monk stepped forward and said, "With intention before the wind, there is no sound within the phrase. The Master said, "Rarely heard from ancient times to the present.
The monk said, "If one encounters a true知音 (one who understands), all is poured forth. The Master said, "Shouldering the whole body [of the Dharma]. The monk said, "From of old..."
[The monk] refused to accept the Master’s instruction. The Master said, “One who kills must repay with his life; one who owes money must repay with the principal.

The monk asked, “If one speaks in this manner, what then? The Master said, “I have already anticipated that there would be no connection. The monk asked, “Does a good spiritual friend not possess skillful means?”

The Master said, "Why trouble yourself to bring it up again? The monk stepped forward and asked, "If someone were to suddenly ask the Master, 'What is the mouth of a true teacher of goodness (śāstrācārya)?
what would you say? The Master said, "I am not a teacher of goodness; from where would I have a mouth? The monk bowed. Thereupon, he cited the Elder Xiangyan’s address to the assembly:

"It is like a man climbing a tree, holding a branch in his mouth" (the Master said, "A wild donkey or a dog tramples him down"). "The branch is broken, and he falls to the ground. (The Master said...)

"This is the floral retribution. (The Master said: "Sitting alone. "The hands do not grasp the branches. (The Master said: "Sitting alone. "The feet do not tread upon the branches. (The Master said: "Lying down alone.

Suddenly, while under the tree, someone asks: (The Master said: "Stop! Stop! "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? (The Master said: "Entering the Sangha Hall via the main path.

To answer would be to lose one's body and life. (The Master said: "Three thousand in the morning. Not to answer would be to violate the questioner's intent. (The Master said: "Eight hundred in the evening. At such a time—
"How is it? (The Master then gave a single shout of acknowledgment and said, "The officials and their retinue are at peace. He spoke again:
"Before the assembly had yet met me, I, this mountain monk, had already met you all while atop the tree.
Now, return to me before I climbed the tree—Upāli, when it was thus, what would you have said? *Duh!* The celestial deities return to heaven; the earth spirits return to earth."
The land is returned; the money is returned to the treasury; the horse is returned to its stall. The disciple expresses gratitude and prostrates with sincere devotion.
May both former intentions and future vows be fully realized, so that on other days and at other times, there shall be no further debt or deficiency.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "Yangqi asked Ciming, 'When the dark birds warble their cries and leave the clouds to enter the jumbled peaks, what then?
Ciming replied, 'I am walking through the wild weeds; you, moreover, have entered a deep village. What is the meaning of this? The Master said:
"Patting is the command. The student said, "Today the Master has leaked the celestial mechanism (*tianji*). The Master said, "Head straight, tail straight.
The student said, "Yangqi said, 'The official does not allow even a needle. If I were to ask further, what would you say?
The Master said, "When one's strength is exhausted, the mountain is even better. The student said, "Ciming gave two successive shouts; what did Yangqi see?"
The student bowed in accordance with propriety. The Master said, "Brandishing weapons, he establishes Great Peace.

The student stepped forward and said, "If so, then the flowers are fundamentally brilliant and the tiger’s coat is originally striped. The Master said, "Who dares to look upon it? The student said, "I thank the Master for his reply. The Master said, "A cat!
Then he cited the story of Gold Peak (Jin-feng) Worthy: One day, a monk came to pay his respects, and Gold Peak asked, "Where have you come from?"
[The monk] approaches. After a long silence, Feng says, "Whom have you come to see? The monk says, "What bowl would I go to see? Feng says, "I, the old monk, am at fault.
The monk says, "It is so, it is so. Feng remains silent for a long while. The Master [Zhaozhou] says, "In one sense, this is like a dragon’s roar raising mist and a tiger’s cry stirring the wind;
there are those who hit the mark and those who do not. This is for those of long-standing study."
"Scholars, try to settle this and look closely.
Entering the hall, [the Master said: "Today is the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month; as before, the eyes are horizontal and the nose is straight. Gather it all up from the very beginning."
It is just like a troupe of miscellaneous plays; they smear themselves with dust and ash. Who among them do I know?
Nine hundred performers, great and small, whose every movement is dictated by their ranks. Suddenly appearing before the stage, they know how to bow and exchange greetings.
When the camels rise up, they strike as they please; when they lower their heads, they weep as they please. Then, suddenly, they let out a cold laugh.
"Laughing until the judge collapses fifty times. If someone were to ask Elder Xiatang, "What about it?
and he were not one to feign madness, he would simply say to him: "The speaker speaks; the listener listens. The seated rise; the walking stand.
If you treat people this way when explaining Chan, what juice are you seeking in a sesame cake?
The Record of the Dharma Talks at Fushan Hongfu Chan Monastery in Taizhou, compiled by the student Ruben.
Opening the Hall. A monk asked: "Manjusri is the teacher of the seven Buddhas; why was he unable to emerge from the woman’s samādhi?"

The Master said, "Wait until you cannot [bear it] anymore. The student stepped forward and asked, "Why was it that Wuming was able to come out? The Master said, "A slave sees his mistress and acts with earnest devotion.
He then said: "My dream-soul flies on the mendicant's staff down to Tiantai; I suspect he has come from another realm to receive offerings."
The stone chamber has suddenly returned to the chill of the mist; the wind and moon of the sea mountains fill the towers and terraces. Thus it is said:
"Where the patch-robed monk walks, a single drop of water turns to ice; a fragment of cloud does not obstruct the vast sky; all waters cannot escape the reflection of the moon.
When one’s feet stand solitary and remote, and the mind is steep and majestic—precisely at such a time, one recalls dwelling at Guoqing in the past.
The temple now occupies the summit of Mount Fushan. How do you express this in a single phrase? [He] pats his knee once and says:
"The misty trees come over; the misty trees receive them. The fine mountains are cast aside; the fine mountains welcome them."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Venerable Zhaozhou. Every time a monk came, he would ask, "Have you been here before?

If the monk said, "I have been here," Zhaozhou would say, "Go drink tea. Again, he asked another monk, "Have you been here before? [The monk replied,] "I have not been here. [Zhaozhou said,] "Go drink tea.
The temple administrator asked, "If one who has been here drinks tea, why does one who has not been here also drink tea? Zhaozhou...
He called out, "Head of the Monastery! The Head responded, "Yes? The Master said, "Go drink tea.
The Teacher remarked, "This old fellow not only washes his face in a long-flowing stream and suns his back upon the altar where offerings are made;

he even treats the public highway as a personal favor and invites guests to the unobstructed kitchen. Do you wish to know where this old fellow has landed? Whether one has arrived or not, everyone drinks tea."
It is not that the eyes bloom with flowers when the lips are moistened. If one is a guest on the boat of the Xie family, would they ever deign to wade through the plains to scoop for fish and shrimp?
Entering the hall, [the Master] raised the case: Jingqing asked a monk, "What is that sound outside the door? The monk said, "The sound of raindrops. Jingqing said, "The assembly..."
The monk said, "One gives rise to perversion; deluded by oneself, one pursues external objects. Dongshan said, "How about you, Master? Qing said, "I have not, in fact, been deluded by myself.
The monk said, "If you have not been deluded by yourself, what is the meaning of that? Qing said, "To emerge from the body may be easy;

to speak the Way from the very core of one's being is difficult. The Master said, "O Great Assembly! People of this day all say that Qing’s tongue has bone in it and that his breath spews wind and clouds."
Zhe’s eyes were blind and his body was covered in mud and water; he did not realize that these two fellows’ money showed no trace and their silver showed no gleam.

On the day [of the ceremony], he ascended the hall: "A single rain washes the plains and fields; A thousand mountains lock in the colors of cold. There is no need to discuss what this matter is: Originally, Hu’s mouth was too narrow. He ascended the hall:
"In the middle of the eleventh month, the deep winter; In this chilly place, look quickly with your own eyes. When spring comes, the grasses and trees turn green again."
When winter passes, the ice and frost melt of their own accord. Who would have known that two five-hundred [coins] originally combine to form one thousand?
Even if it were refined gold of a hundred smeltings, it must still enter the red furnace for further forging. Once forged, what then?
A mirror of ancient rhombus-patterned glass suddenly emerges from the humble gate—far surpassing the *chē-dù* drill of the Qin era.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] cited the story of Dayu taking leave of Guizong. Guizong asked, "Where are you going? Dayu replied, "I am going to study the 'five flavors' of Chan in various quarters.
Guizong said, "I also have this 'one flavor' of Chan here. Dayu asked, "What is the Master’s one-flavor Chan?
Guizong then struck him. Dayu said, "I understand! Guizong said, "Speak! Speak! As Dayu was about to open his mouth, Guizong struck him again.
[The Master] struck him and drove him out of the hall. The Master said: "If one follows the law to its full extent, there will be no subjects left.
One man runs horses upon ice; another lays his body across the edge of a sword. Even if you examine this closely, what advantage is there for you?
Do you all wish to see where these two old fellows have fallen? Listen to this verse: The secret instructions of the immortals are wondrous and difficult to transmit. [Bald-headed... "
The head asura strikes his left fist; returning at midnight, there is no place to be found. Starving, he lies high upon his bed beside the rice basket.
Entering the hall, a monk asked: "When the crows cry and the magpies screech, every dharma is perfectly accomplished. Seeing is the same seeing; hearing is the same hearing."
"Why is there delusion and why is there awakening? The Master said, "Recalling the power of Avalokiteśvara; both sides are without concern.
The student further asked, "Setting aside seeing and hearing, do you permit the student to pursue this further? The Master said, "Who taught you to thrust your brain into a glue pot?
The student said, "Buying iron and obtaining gold—a great fortune indeed! The Master said, "I have answered your question; I expected as much."
Beyond the reach of agitation or submersion, he said: "The alms bowl contains the world; the staff stirs the vast ocean.

Fish and dragons alike leave no trace; even Buddhas and Patriarchs flee their forms. At midday, the total function is revealed; the crow has sunk, the sun has not yet risen. In autumn, the mountain moon is white;
when spring arrives, the scorched earth turns green."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Chan Master Dongyan Kehou. One day, as he was descending from the abbot’s quarters, he saw Dongshan approaching.
Looking at him, Kehou asked, “Where are you going? Dongshan said, “I am going to pay my respects. Kehou said, “Why are you wandering about aimlessly?
Dongshan said, “I am away for a moment. Kehou said, “Where have you gone? Xuedou commented, “He should have been given thirty blows.”
[He] struck him with the staff. The Master said, "If you possess the diamond eye, let me ask you: where do these thirty blows fall? On the guest? On the host?

Xuedou [then] took them upon himself. "If you can see through this, not only will my old monk’s meditation seat tremble, but all people throughout the great earth will have frost in their mouths. Now, how would you deal with it? [With this, he] waved his whisk once.
[The Master] struck [the meditation seat] and said: "At twilight on the sands, wild geese take flight; flying crosswise and slantwise, they enter the sea gates.

He ascended the hall and, citing the Venerable Yunju You’s address to the assembly, said: "Students who study the Way must attain enlightenment within awakening and bring forth clarity regarding the mind-ground.
If you awaken to the Lord of the Dharmakāya, then all the grasses and trees throughout the great earth will take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. If you awaken..."
Vairocana. Throughout the worlds of empty space, one takes refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. But tell me: what do you call the "Master of the Dharmakāya"?
What do you call "Vairocana"? Do you wish to understand this directly? Within the eyes, light is emitted and auspicious signs appear;
within the ear-cavities, the Great Dharma Wheel turns. The Master said: "The Great Assembly, Vairocana has no teacher. What do you call..."
"Vairocana! Is it within the ear-cavities that you turn the Great Dharma Wheel? The Dharmakāya has no master;
what do you call the 'master of the Dharmakāya'? Is it within the eyes that you emit light and manifest auspicious omens?

A peaked-roof hat, a nose-cutting hemp sandal, a collarless cotton shirt, and a waistband with its strap severed—you are accustomed to wearing them sideways or upside down, naturally possessing a singular style."
How elegant! Even if one were to smear oneself with forest soil and ashes, there would ultimately be no difference between the two categories.
What do you all call the "Lord of the Dharma-body"? What do you call the "Vairocana Teacher"? At this very moment, how is it?
If you can understand, let these thirty blows be exposed to the sun and wind. If you cannot understand, look at the cold pines and right-side junipers.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring days linger on; the spring breeze sweeps vast. Green waters wind around its waist; green mountains wear their caps.
Willows are verdant, flowers are red; crows cry and magpies clamor. The Great Gate of Generosity stands open—where can one find a place to enter?
He gave a shout and said: "Wang Yizhi’s cursive calligraphy has entered the stone three inches deep. Do you all see Deshan, Linji, Nanquan, and Zhaozhou?"
May all universally turn from heterodoxy and enter the Right Path.
[The Master] ascends the hall and cites the case of Guishan asking National Teacher Xiuxi: "When sound and form are pure and true, what is the Way? Xiuxi said:
"What are you doing, disturbing the Way? Guishan then walked from east to west. Xuefeng said, "If you do not act thus, it will be a disaster.

Guishan then walked from west to east and stood still. As Xuefeng stepped down from his rope seat and had just taken two steps, Gushan grabbed him and asked, "What is the matter of sound and form being pure and true?
Xuefeng then gave him a slap. Guishan said, "Ten years hence, you will need someone..."
The man said, "There is no tea here. Xuefeng said, "What do you want with the old fellow from Gushan?
Gushan laughed heartily three times. The Master said, "Tell me, where does his point lie? Why did he laugh only three times and not four?
Those who possess the eyes of a true student—can they discern this? Gold is tested by stone; jade is tested by fire."
He blocked the three sounds. "What do you all use to test [this]? Is it not like this: "If one does not sleep in the same bed, how can one know the lining of the quilt is worn through?
I knew early on that you had misunderstood; listen to this verse: When two armies clash, laughter seems like anger; The eyebrows stand upright, and sinews form in the eyes.
With whom shall the streams, mountains, clouds, and moon be companions? North, south, east, and west—utterly cut off.
At Jinlin, a donor invited the Master to ascend the hall. A monk asked, "Regarding the treasury of the true Dharma-eye and the wondrous mind of nirvana, how is it to be utilized?
The Master said, "Handed over with both hands. The monk pressed further, "What is it like when one understands it in this very way? The Master said, "A mute person eating."
Bitter Melon. Jìn said, "A man of clarity does not perform obscure deeds. The Master said, "If one wishes to take something away, one must first firmly give it to him.
Jìn said, "Yesterday someone came from Chen Prefecture and went toward Xu Prefecture. The Master said, "Apart from this."
"Speak another word! The monk stepped forward and gave a shout. The Master said, "Press on! The monk bowed. The Master then said:
"Xu Tinggan of Jianshan requested me three times to discourse on Prajñā. Before even crossing the gate of Fushan, it was all spoken at once.
Furthermore, I have opened up the heavenly mouth and blocked the vast void. To the south of Tan and north of Xiang, west of Zhaozhou."
To the east of the monastery, he casts down a vajra-ring; furthermore, there are more than hundreds of thousands of *liji* thorns. Swallowing and leaping over them is endless.
Fortunately, there is the perilous cliff-phrase right before one’s eyes; this mountain monk does not dare to add another commentary.
The qilin laughs at the moon, piercing the heavens; the clay ox pulls up the coral tree.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Master Langya Jue, who cited the former Master Liangshan’s address to the assembly: “To those coming from the south, I give thirty blows;
to those coming from the north, I give thirty blows. Although it is so, this does not accord with the essence of the school. Langya said:
Liangshan: "What a piece of pure gold! To sell it as common iron! Langlang, however, would not have it so:
thirty blows for those coming from the south, thirty blows for those coming from the north—let the monks of the world criticize him as they will.
The Master said: "Those two old fellows—one hides his body while revealing his shadow; the other reveals his shadow while hiding his body. I, this mountain monk, am not like that.
To those from the south, I give a ladle of salty, sour, and vinegar-flavored soup; to those from the north, I give a ladle of bitter greens and plain radish broth."
If you eat, you will strike the upright because of the crooked; if you do not eat, you will wander aimlessly from east to west.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Baizhang asking Zhaozhou, "Where have you recently come from? Zhaozhou replied, "From Nanquan. Baizhang asked, "What words did Nanquan speak?
Zhaozhou said, "To those who have not yet attained it, one must simply remain silent. Baizhang then gave a shout, and Zhaozhou acted as if frightened.
Baizhang said, "How wonderful, how profoundly silent! Thereupon, Zhaozhou performed a dance and departed. The Master said, "What a pity to let him go! But tell me, whom did I let go?
Did I let Zhaozhou go, or did I let Baizhang go? The ancients had a single turning phrase, which was like a single eye.
As for you all, you will surely be like a head stuck in a vat of glue; you will inevitably say it was Zhaozhou."
He performed a dance and departed. Baizhang remained silent; thus, he did not let him off the hook. "Fortunately, there is no connection," [Baizhang] said after a long while.
"There is a gate within the gate, and a gate without the gate. One does not act like Yan Ping offending the Ox and Dipper constellations.
A lion frowns while a jackal howls. Plucking out the pupils from the eyes of Li Lou. Extending one hand and contracting the other. Double Ninth is definitely in the ninth month."
Nine. Turning over seas and mountains to seek a kindred spirit, bare-boned strength exhausted, both elbows exposed.
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Chan Master Nanluohan of Luohan Temple, who addressed the assembly, saying: "Red clouds pierce the azure void; white egrets dot the blue marshes.
Were it not for Hanshan, at this moment he would be standing by an ancient ford. Riding a fine steed, galloping atop a high tower, ten thousand miles of silver."
Rolling a jade ball down a river—another name for "true liberation. Poking at fire to seek bubbles—The Master said, "This old fellow!
When it comes to speaking the Way, he only manages eighty percent. Not only does he hand the ladder to the thief, he is also the one who reaps what he sows.
This mountain monk, while walking along, casually mimicked his frown and presents this to the great assembly: Crimson clouds pierce the azure void; white egrets...
Dew forms upon the moss. Failing to capture the head of Yan Liang, who could truly exclaim "How wonderful!"? The roots emerge from the tips of the branches;
the fruit opens from within the flowers. This very thing requires no guessing: green mountains and blue waters are right at one's temples.
Sometimes they cannot be found; yet they return just as they were.
Ascending the hall: On the eighth day of the fourth month of that year, the old illness of the Barbarian [Buddha] flared up again. When Yunmen encountered water, he took off his shoes;
do not follow along with Dharma Master Mengba. The nine dragons spewed water to bathe his golden body, yet even his seven steps of circumambulation were not as good as this.
I prostrate and take refuge in the dry dung-stick. A beardless barbarian further collides with a red-bearded barbarian.
Entering the hall: It has already been half a month since the summer retreat began. How is it that the deity of Kapilavastu and the Jiang Temple are contending for the mountain?
This mountain monk first recalls that before I left the household life, one year was better than one month, and one month was better than...

One day is better than one hour; once one has left the household life, one year is not equal to one month, one month is not equal to one day, and one day is not equal to one hour. Even though this is so, tell me, people:
is it that which is superior, or is it that which is inferior? Wildfire cannot burn it away; the spring breeze blows and it grows again.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an example from Zhenjing, who said to the assembly: "Under the gate of Dongshan, if you wish to walk, you walk; if you wish to sit, you sit.
To defecate in the alms bowl and spit into the water pitcher while adhering to the Dharma and practicing cultivation is like an ox pulling a millstone. The Master said:
This is indeed so. It is far too unapproachable for human sentiment. How does it compare to the school of Fushan, which does not permit squatting?
They burn the fields within the eyes and grind flour within the nostrils. Whether it be a Buddha or an Ancestor arriving, they spit right in their faces—even if one should not spit, they must spit.
Why is this so? Look at the man who draws his bow; he is no match for the one who shoots the target.
Ascending the hall on account of a matter: The waters are full and the flowers lush; spring is at its height. The Lord of the East stirs my weary heart with intent.
Whether the customs elsewhere match those of our Sichuan remains uncertain, But the fragrance of lychees is already perceived by the sense of smell.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Mañjuśrī exhausted all his strength with a single question; Vimalakīrti was left tongue-tied and speechless.布袋 (Bùdài) wandered aimlessly for a long time;
Kāśyapa sat in meditation for kalpas. The nostrils are right upon the face; the lips never leave the mouth.
Four coins make two; three coins yield one. Now, subtracting the principal from the interest, we are glad that both principal and interest remain."
Having displayed them all, he then pointed with his staff and said, "Assembly, this is the water pitcher; that is the incense burner.
What is the fundamental? Let us strike the drum and invite everyone to look! He then cast down the staff.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What was the intent behind Danxia burning the wooden Buddha? The Master said, "If there were no charcoal in the monks' hall, say it once.
The monk stepped forward and asked, "What would you have me say? The Master said, "Overhead it is vast;
beneath one's feet it is vast. The Master then cited the scripture: "This seeing and its conditions are originally the wondrous, pure, and luminous Bodhi."
The Master said, "Wrong. Yunfeng Yue Heshang said, "The ancient sages entered the void and extended their hands, skillfully opening up expedient means."
The Master said, “Wrong. He spoke again, “If you can understand my two wrongs, I will join hands with you and ascend the high peak.
If you do not understand, feel free to walk alone through the crimson heavens. Even so, you must still examine this closely.

After a long silence, he said, “If you understand these two wrongs of Fushan, the Buddhas and Patriarchs will have their scaffolding dismantled from the start. If you remain as you were before, it is all in vain.”

When the monk Jihuang (Extremely Yellow) was about to ascend the hall, a white crane flew over. A monk asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? The Master said, "Ha! Why did you not ask sooner?"
The monk hesitated. The Master struck him and said: "A single phrase pierces through the mountains and seas, shaking heaven and earth.
As for the matter at the very bottom of the alms bowl—how is it? A single phrase: the eyes empty the four seas, ten thousand miles of cloudless sky.
Bring forth that one phrase from the tip of the staff! After a long silence, he raised his staff, struck once, and departed. Brightness and darkness, form and emptiness.
Completely exposed. Coming and going, appearing and disappearing, they are not mutually related.
[The Master] ascends the hall: "If one can depart from all marks, one immediately enters the Dharma King’s house.
The Dharma King has no dual dharmas; the absence of dharma is itself the house. Therefore, the Dharma of the Dharma King is like a bitter gourd."

Ascending the hall, he said: "Clouds enshroud the mountain peaks; the moon reflects in the heart of the waves. Private roads admit neither carriage nor horse; official gates do not permit even a needle.
Those who have attained it may rest as they please; those who have not attained it may likewise rest as they please. A tiger cub and a dragon foal; a rabbit’s head sprouting horns.
Spring light and night rain, sunny days—fear not that they will rot to the very root."
Ascending the hall, he said: Outside the gate, spring is already half-way through; Rock flowers bloom amidst the rain. Faith arrives from beyond the heavens;

People come from the side of the sun. The tiger roars and wind arises in the valley; The dragon sings and mist fills his whiskers. Meeting face to face, brows cover eyes; On level ground, they dance the Three Terraces.

[The student] said, “I understand. [The Master asked,] “If you do not discern the true reality, what is your intention? The Master said, “A cotton-wrapped hammer.
[The student] advanced and said, “Today the Master has spoken with his whole mouth. The Master said, “Damo sat facing the wall for nine years; how would you deal with that?
[The student] advanced and said, “Opened wide with eight characters, handed over with both hands. The Master said, “You have missed it beneath your own heels. Why is this so?”
"I do not know. The monk stepped forward and said, "In the clear blue sky and bright daylight, what fault is there? The Master said, "Not yet. Speak further.
As the monk prepared to open his mouth, the Master said, "I told you it was 'not yet. The monk was speechless.
The Master then said: "Empty... [text missing] ...the public case has not been brought forth for examination since the time of the Seven Buddhas.
As for the appearance of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, how many people have misunderstood it!
Even now, they are mistaken—and having made this mistake, how can one avoid this fault? Even if one’s faculty were like a flash of lightning and one’s eyes like..."
A shooting star! He emerges wearing a rabbit’s head, knocking off his shackles and breaking his chains.

No need for even a single note. Why? Zen is not of thought; the Way is beyond achievement. Zen is not Zen; the Way is not the Way. When both Zen and the Way are negated, what is it? After a long silence, he said:
"The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horn from gazing at the moon; the elephant sprouts eight tusks when startled by thunder."
[The Master] raised this case [and further received an imperial decree ordering him to judge a koan].
The Master then cited Master Qianfeng’s address to the assembly, saying: "The Dharma-body has three kinds of illness and two kinds of light.

Only when each of these is thoroughly penetrated can one sit securely. Furthermore, you must know there is the simultaneous application of illumination and function, where both person and environment are seized."

At that moment, when the "upper orifice" was present, Master Yunmen stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "Why does the person inside the hermitage not know what is happening outside the hermitage?
Qianfeng laughed heartily. Yunmen said, "This is still a point of doubt for students.
Qianfeng said, "What kind of mental activity is yours? Yunmen replied, "I also wish for the Master to share in this understanding."
Xiqian said, "You must act exactly like this before you can sit securely. Yunmen responded, "Yes, yes. The Master commented: "True enough.
One man displays the strategic maneuvers of a celestial being; the other possesses the divine mechanism that spans the sea.
But do they truly capture that single aperture of the 'transcendental' realm where illumination and function are simultaneous, and both person and environment are seized? As for the Dharma-body..."
"What is illness? To study [the teachings] is illness. He further said, "There are two kinds of light.
As for mountains, rivers, the great earth, and the moon reflected in water—what fault is there in these? Now, do you wish to see where the two elders fell? The Master then offered this verse:
Within the hermitage, one knows not the affairs outside; Iron-faced and bronze-headed, they are not alike. Upon the fixed flower-board, they swing the swing.
The fierce tiger’s tongue writes the *svastika* character. After the Master had ascended the seat and finished his expression of gratitude for the imperial favor, he submitted this memorial, saying:
"I, your subject, have previously been summoned by Your Majesty for an audience; I hereby respectfully record and present it."
The Emperor said, "Excellent, excellent.
As soon as the Master received it, he tossed it onto the ground and asked for it again.
The Master replied, "This is like a lion’s somersault; it can only save half."
The Emperor said, "In my domain, there is not even a single character. The Master replied, "Alas, when cast upon the ground, it makes the sound of gold.
Chaner (Zhanei) added from behind, "It has already spread throughout the world."
The Emperor laughed heartily. The Master then expressed his gratitude and descended from the hall.
