Imperial Decree: The Dharma-Transmitting Great Master Fohai (Huiyuan), Abbot of Lingyin Chan Temple in Jingde, is hereby specially granted the title of Chan Master Fohai.
Upon receiving the imperial edict and returning to the temple, he shall face the palace and express his gratitude for the imperial favor.

Ten edicts descended from the Celestial Book; boundless grace flew down from the Nine Palaces. The myriad realms have returned to the orthodox transformation; once in a thousand years, such a meeting occurs.
(Your servant) Cao Fu is filled with shame; his binding of bamboo strips is unworthy. Amidst cold fires and deep smoke, the late years of his life see the embers of frost rise into flame.
As vast as heaven and earth, this remaining life—a withered stump—returns to spring. Having humbly received the Imperial Grace, he is specially bestowed with the title of Chan Master.

[Your] title. With ninefold prostrations, I bow my head; with focused and sincere resolve, I, the humble monk Huiyuan, am overwhelmed by my deepest feelings as I gaze upon Heaven and look toward the Sage.
My agitation and trepidation are most intense and earnest.

Ascending the hall, he held up the incense and said: "This single offering of incense transcends Buddhas and patriarchs and stands far beyond heaven and earth. From it, all moving beings and sentient creatures are brought forth;
by it, the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are established. Now, as I burn this within the burner, I reverently offer it for the long life and prosperity of [the Imperial Court]."
Long life to His Majesty the Emperor. Long life to His Majesty the Retired Emperor,
Glorious and August, Constitutionally Holy, and Embodiment of the Way of Heaven.
To the Longevity-Sage Empress Dowager, the Empress, and the Imperial Consorts; to the celestial kin of the two palaces; and to His Imperial Highness the Crown Prince:

We reverently pray that the jade leaves may long remain fragrant, that you may uphold the divine vessel to once again open the realm under heaven, and that with the golden wheel as your sovereign, you may establish the ancestral temple to restore the era of Great Peace. Thereafter, may you expand the frontiers of the three borders and clear away all disturbances.

Throughout the four seas, with ten winds and five rains, may earth and heaven endure for a long time. May your longevity be as high as Mount Sumeru, and your merit as deep and far-reaching as the Ganges River.
The Master took his seat and said: "Like lightning rolling and stars racing—those who are true practitioners know this. Applying it upside down and using it in reverse, he sharply rouses the mind.
The frost-flowered precious sword is leveled against the wind; the wrathful Nanda and Upananda peer with brows furrowed.

Is there any monk—a patch-robed one who, while walking along, casually swings his arm and immediately boards the boat—who can come forth and provide evidence? A monk asked: "The purple-clay imperial decree has arrived from the Nine Palaces."
Auspicious light pervades the earth, impossible to part; at the head of Buddhas and Patriarchs, he issues his true command. Within the eye of a gnat, he performs the Three Terraces dance.
At such a time as this, what is the single phrase for repaying kindness? The Master said: "Spiritual powers vast and great; transformations without end. The monk said:
"The multitudes of devas and humans all receive the power of this grace. The Master said: "The staff remains as it was before."
"It is black as lacquer. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "A mute man eating bitter melon. The monk asked, "Where are the eyes of a good spiritual friend?
The Master said, "This fellow has defeated himself before he was even examined. The monk prostrated; the Master said, "Many fine days together."
Again, a monk asked: "A tiger-token hangs upon his body; the eight *vajra*-guardians raise aloft the banner that covers heaven.
An iron covenant accompanies him; the four heavenly kings firmly hold the seal of Vairocana. He subdues the ninety-six kinds of non-Buddhists and destroys the eighty-four thousand armies of Māra.
I bow my head before the Great Zen Master of the Buddha-ocean; to repay your vast kindness, please speak of the Non-dual. What is this Non-dual?"
The Master said, "In the city of Vaiśālī, the canopies were just lowered; on Vulture Peak, the events remain as they were.
The monk said, "As Śūnyatā-janman sat by the cliffside, celestial flowers came from the earth. The Master said, "I shall grant you this for the merit of your vegetarian feast and repentance.
The monk said, "If that is so, then the great assembly shall receive your grace. The Master said, "What about the matter prior to the seven Buddhas?"
The monk hesitated to speak. The Master then gave a shout. The monk bowed. Another monk asked: "Auspicious vapors and auspicious clouds pervade the nine realms;
the Chan Master’s illustrious title comes from the side of the sun. How shall one repay such towering sagely virtue? Amidst the flash of lightning, you thunder the Dharma drum.
At this very moment, I ask the Master to answer. The Master said: "A sudden clap of thunder leaves no time to cover one's ears. The monk [bowed].
The monk said, "If that is so, then wind follows the tiger and clouds follow the dragon. The Master said, "Two colors, one match.

The monk said, "When the Master answers a question like this, it makes all bystanders laugh. The Master said, "An army marches by deceptive paths. The monk said, "It is better to let a thief go than to catch him.
The Master said, "What are you saying? The monk was speechless and then prostrated himself. The Master then said, "Nine years of sitting in cold seclusion."

Once, with eyes fixed upon the clouds and sky, a single staff flew hither. Who would have looked at that tongue trailing on the ground? Deceiving Buddhas and Patriarchs with hot lies, you sneered at the monks;
knowing only how to cover your nose while stealing fragrance, you did not realize you were vainly inviting transgression.

Fortunately, having encountered the Sagely Sovereign, I was granted the sight of his pure radiance. Having mistakenly received the immense bounty of the sovereign’s cloud-like grace, I was specially bestowed the title of "Chan Master Fohai."

The title [is set]. Mountains and rivers grow more magnificent; the sun of wisdom shines once more. Before the imperial pavilion, the true command is fully upheld; atop the golden hall, the bell suddenly awakens.
There has never been any deficiency. The four seas are not too many. The mirror of wisdom is penetratingly clear;
the flower of the mind blooms brilliantly. The West River is sucked dry; the Northern Dipper is laid across the body. At such a time, how is it? Have you not seen it? [The] Monk.
A question was asked of Master Touzi: "What is the Tamer of the Ten Bodies? Touzi descended from his meditation seat, joined his palms, and stood there.
Now, as for Touzi’s descending from the seat and standing with palms joined—tell me, what is the essential principle here?
"When there is nothing to do, beat the drum; everyone is invited to look. Furthermore, it is not unlike when Emperor Suzong asked National Teacher Zhong: "What is..."
"The Ten-Body Tamer. The National Teacher said, "Donor, you are treading upon the crown of Vairocana's head. The Emperor said, "I do not understand.
The National Teacher said, "Your Majesty, do not mistakenly identify this as your own pure *dharmakāya*.
The assembly, tell me: how far apart are the pure *dharmakāya* and the Ten-Body Tamer? If you can distinguish between them, you will still not avoid being caught in the sleeve.
"Head to collar. If you do not distinguish between the monastic and the lay, you will inevitably have to cut away the lapel from under your arm.
Now, suppose someone were to ask, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer at Lingyin? and I were to lift the corner of my *kāṣāya* and say, "Do you understand?
This is what I won at the foot of the Dragon Bed of the Sacred Son of Heaven. Today, I shall not refuse to give it to you."
To leak out the celestial mechanism is to universally show all people that they have already attained realization. But tell me, how do you prove this for yourselves?
[The Master] throws down the corner of his *kāṣāya* and says: "Perfect mechanisms are chanted in mutual resonance, transcending names and models;
wondrous responses are like turning a waterwheel. The source of Beiji flows to the coastal mountains; the branches of Xiqi flourish across rivers and lakes. One phrase—thoroughly penetrated."

The Celestial Highway: Grasses, trees, insects, and fish transform according to their nature; mountains, rivers, seas, and peaks also join in joyful acclaim. The great trichiliocosm returns to the Enlightened Sovereign;
ten thousand nations bring tribute by land and sea to the Imperial Capital. Having long established the multitude in compassion, we humbly pray that you will cherish yourself.
The assembly descends from their seats.
A Memorial of Thanks for the Special Bestowal of the Title of Chan Master Fohai as Abbot of Jingde Lingyin Chan Temple by His Subject and Monk Huiyuan, the Dharma-transmitter.
On the thirtieth day of this month,
we reverently received the Imperial Decree that Huiyuan, the Abbot and Dharma-transmitting Great Master Fohai of Jingde Lingyin Chan Monastery,
shall be specially granted the title of Chan Master Fohai. We, the monk Huiyuan, have already led the assembly to welcome him on that very day.
The imperial edict returned to the temple. [The recipient] gazed toward the palace to express gratitude for the imperial favor, and having completed the formal reception, [submitted this report].
Right: (Your servant) has heard by hearsay that during the reign of the Benevolent Emperor, the Way held Huailian in high esteem and bestowed upon him the title "Dajue";
during the reign of Deshou, the grace toward Foguo was profound and he changed his appellation to "Yuanwu. Having once again received the gracious hearing of Your Majesty, [the titles were] advanced.

(Your Servant), the Chan monk Fohai, has received the grace that descends from the Nine Heavens. It is a fortunate occasion to have encountered this millennium. (Your Servant) prostrates himself with utmost sincerity and trepidation.

I humbly consider that while the non-establishment of views and hearing transcends verbal expression, the full manifestation of names and principles accords with the wondrous beginning, harmonizing essence and function. Therefore, there are both canons and regulations; how could one not treat them as vessels?
Yet this is not called the nobility of the Way; it is the inclusion of those with appropriate talent through careful selection. I humbly reflect:

(Your Servant) donned the three robes in my youth, yet in old age I lack even an inch of merit. As a subject of the enlightened people of Yao and Shun, I am a descendant of the lineage of the Patriarchs and Masters.
How could I have hoped that in these declining white hairs, I would behold Your Majesty’s profound and pure radiance, and move Your Dragon-like countenance with a single smile?
In truth, the Revival of the Image-Dharma has flourished, yet I have held office at a great monastery and thus harbor the shame of one carrying a burden he cannot bear.
Now that I am invested with this illustrious name, how can I avoid the reproach of seeking it by mere chance? This grace bestowed upon me is unsurpassed; to receive it fills me with awe.
Considering my own mediocrity and folly, how could I ever be worthy of such patronage? It is now my good fortune to encounter Your Majesty, the Emperor, whose Way transcends the four great elements.
His virtue surpasses that of a hundred kings. With his sagely mind, he is in perfect accord with the heart-essence of the ancient Buddhas;

with his celestial eye, he penetrates the Treasury of the True Dharma-Eye. He sports in the samādhis of *yōgyū* (liberated play) and attends to myriad affairs while presiding over the golden wheel as the honored sovereign of ten thousand chariots. Yet, he still bears in mind that single word from Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa.
Submitted. Thus, even those recluses who crouch and hide within mountain forests have likewise received their transformation within the furnace of Heaven and Earth.
How could we dare not steadfastly maintain *dhyāna* and diligently practice the precepts? Though the mountains are long and the waters are distant, we respectfully offer our call from Mount Song;
may the earth turn and heaven revolve, so that we may obtain the treasure of the Central Plains. We respectfully present this memorial.
Expressing gratitude for this announcement: (Your servant) Huiyuan, with utmost humility and trepidation, bows his head repeatedly and respectfully submits these words.
On the [day] of the tenth month in the eighth year of the Qiandao era, the Buddha-Sea Chan Master was specially bestowed the appointment as Abbot of Jingde Chan Monastery.
Memorial Submitted by the Dharma-transmitting Subject Monk Huiyuan:
To Bestow Special Favor upon Chan Master Fohai to Reside at Lingyin.
Record of the Imperial Audience, compiled respectfully by the Subject Monk Attendant. Recorded and Presented for Imperial Inspection.
On the twentieth day of the first month in the seventh year of the Qiandao era,
an imperial decree was issued ordering Huiyuan to be presented for an audience on the following day; furthermore,
another decree was issued for the twenty-third day.
The Emperor returned from his visit to Deśou Palace and summoned [the Master] for an audience. That day, he entered Seondeokjeon Hall for the formal interview.
The Master addressed him, saying: "Your servant was born in Meishan in Western Sichuan. I have been traveling abroad for over forty years;
while among the mountains and forests, I have heard only..."
Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, you have responded to the myriad affairs of state daily; your Way surpasses that of a thousand ages.
You externally protect the Buddha-Dharma, in perfect harmony with the dragons and devas. This is what is called governing the world with a Buddha-mind.
(I, your subject) Kēqín, Dharma-heir of Chan Master Fuguo Yuánwù, was thus addressed. When asked, "Who is Yuánwù?", he replied, "He is my teacher."
When the Emperor, the Great Sovereign, was encamped at Weiyang, he conferred upon him the title of Chan Master Yuanwu.
The Emperor remarked, "While I was in Weiyang, I regretted that I did not get to see the old master Gaofeng.
He replied, "Zonggaofeng and I both emerged from the same lineage as Chan Master Yuanwu. The Emperor asked, "When did you come to Lingyin? He replied, "Last winter."
On the day before the Festival of Celebration, [the subject] entered the temple to sweep and sprinkle it.

Now, once again, he has been favored by Your Majesty’s gracious attention, allowing him to behold Your Majesty’s radiant countenance. My entire family and my teachers alike have received Your Majesty’s sacred grace;

how could we be sufficiently grateful for such an honorable encounter? [The subject] respectfully presents ten previously composed eulogies for Your Majesty’s perusal. Upon their presentation, the Emperor bestowed [a reward].
He sat down. He reported, saying, "In the presence of the Sovereign, how could I dare to sit? The Emperor said, "You are the representative of the elders.
He reported, saying, "I am grateful for Your Majesty’s gracious favor. Please allow me a moment to descend from the hall to express my thanks. Thereupon, he took his seat.
The Emperor asked, "How can one escape birth and death? He replied, "If one does not awaken to the Way of the Mahāyāna, one will ultimately be unable to escape.

The Emperor asked, "How does one attain awakening? He replied, "It is the nature that has been possessed from the beginning; simply polish it with the passage of years and months, and there is no one who will not awaken.
The Emperor asked, "What is it like after awakening? He replied, "Only after awakening does one know."
"What Your Majesty asks and what I have submitted are both entirely incorrect. The Emperor said, "If everything is incorrect, what then?
He replied, "It is manifest before one in its entirety; there is not even a hair’s breadth of a mark to be seen.
The Emperor nodded his head in approval. He continued, "An ancient worthy said: 'To have nothing to which one can point as correct is Bodhi. The Emperor said, "This mind is itself Buddha."
“How is it? he asked. The Master replied, “There is no dharma before one’s eyes; Your Majesty, what do you call ‘mind’? The Emperor asked, “What is mind?
The Master stood with his body upright and hands joined in *añjali*. “It is just this,” he said. The Emperor’s countenance was greatly pleased. The Emperor then questioned him further.

"How were the karmic conditions for the enlightenment of Deshan and Linji? The Master recounted them in detail. The Emperor asked, "To call for 'Xiaoyu' repeatedly is originally a matter of no concern;
it is simply that one wishes the husband to recognize the sound. This is the point attained by Yuanwu; it is merely intended to have people recognize the sound.
[The Emperor] continued, "To call for 'Xiaoyu' repeatedly is originally a matter of no concern; it does not command Xiaoyu to sweep."
Di Jiancha said: "I only want the patron to recognize the sound. Yuanwu used this to question Master Wuzu Yan.
Wuzu said, "This is precisely what is called Chan. Yuanwu asked, "What is Chan? Wuzu raised the case again:
"Frequently calling for Little Yu is originally a matter of no concern; I only want the patron to recognize the sound. "What is the Buddha? Three pounds of flax."
Yuanwu suddenly attained a realization. Wuzu asked again, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Yuanwu replied, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Yuanwu let out a long sigh. Wuzu asked, "How do you understand this?
Yuanwu said, "To cast away the thing within the breast and exhaust all traces before one's eyes. Wuzu said, "This fellow has thoroughly penetrated it. The Emperor remarked, "Excellent."
"Excellent. He reported, "After awakening, ten thousand phrases, a hundred thousand phrases—even the entire Great Canon of the Buddha’s teachings—are but a single phrase.
The Emperor asked, "What is that one phrase? He replied, "Good words do not leave the gate. The Emperor attained silent realization.

He asked again, "Can one who does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion be considered a worthy candidate for study? He replied, "This one question from Old Pang startles heaven and shakes the earth."
[The Master] said, "It drives away mountains and fills the seas; it transcends past and present and is liberated from right and wrong. It is beyond words and cuts off all reliance.
It is just as Your Majesty’s supreme and noble Great Way is fundamentally so. The Emperor said, "It simply does not reside in existence or non-existence.
The Master replied, "Even that which is free from existence and non-existence is not required. The Emperor asked, "What about you, Master? The Master raised his fist.
[The Emperor] said, "I am a man from the wilds (a commoner). My conduct is crude and irregular, and I am ignorant of the rules of propriety.
I beg Your Majesty for leniency. The Emperor said, "That does not hinder you from discussing Chan. He asked again, "Who has attained the Way?

He replied, "As for those who study the Way, according to the depth or shallowness of their capacity, one may verify whether they are people who have entered the inner chamber. They themselves also know the proper timing. For example, once..."
The Emperor addressed Minister Kai, who was also a man close to the Way. The Emperor asked, "Could it be that he was one of those who disagreed with the peace negotiations at the beginning?
Kai replied, "It was indeed he. The Emperor asked, "How did he attain realization? Kai replied, "I once asked him, 'What is a good spiritual friend (śāstrī)?
He answered, 'Even though lanterns, pillars, cats, and dogs are all called good spiritual friends.'"
I asked further: "Master Zeng, since you call yourself a *kalyāṇamitra* (spiritual friend), why is it that you feel joy when praised and affliction when disparaged?
I said: "Have you ever seen a *kalyāṇamitra*, Minister? Zeng said: "I have practiced Chan for thirty years; how could I not have seen one? I said:
"Do you see them in moments of joy, or do you see them in moments of affliction? As Zeng was about to deliberate upon this, I let out a thunderous shout.
[Zhang] was about to open his mouth. [The Subject] said, "The one who opens his mouth is not he. He then became bewildered. [The Subject] asked, "Where has Minister Zeng gone?
Without realizing it, Zeng nodded his head and sighed deeply. [The Subject] said, "I am glad that the Great Matter is now concluded.

Zeng then composed a verse of spontaneous realization, saying: "Alas, this old donkey! A pestilence to the monastic groves. With a single roar that shakes the earth, the celestial mechanism is leaked!"
Someone asked further, "What is your intention? [The Master] raised his whisk and struck him across the mouth. The Emperor said, "Are there any others?

He replied, "In recent times, those who study the Buddha have been numerous, and the opportunities for spiritual encounter have also been extensive. Fearing that it might weary Your Majesty’s hearing, I did not dare report more.
I beg to return to the monastery, where I shall transmit the Mind-Teaching of the Buddha to the monks who come from all quarters, thereby repaying Your Majesty's grace. He then bowed and withdrew.
I pray that Your Majesty will soon restore the Central Plains to pacify the hopes of the four seas.
The Emperor said, “There is more you must say later. He replied, “I shall respectfully withdraw to listen. Having expressed his thanks, he descended from the hall.
Imperial Decree Granting Chan Master Fohai Residency at Lingyin: Record of the Imperial Audience and Discourse.
Compiled respectfully by the attendant-monk, [Name], and presented for imperial inspection on the twenty-eighth day of the first month in the eighth year of the Qiandao era.
The imperial carriage proceeded to Lingyin Monastery. Upon arriving at Cold Spring Pavilion, the Master performed his salutations;
the attending official then transmitted the Imperial decree:
"Venerable Elder, return to the monastery. When the Emperor reached the triple gate, he dismounted from his horse, and the Master again performed his salutations.
The Emperor said, "Let us go; Master, attend me. They proceeded to the front of the Scripture Hall. The Master addressed the Emperor, saying, "The long corridors are high and steep;
I fear they may cause Your Majesty difficulty in walking. The Emperor replied, "It matters not. They then proceeded to the front of the Sangha Hall and entered.
The Master first went to the Abbot’s Quarters (Fangzhang) to burn incense. When the Emperor arrived at the Abbot’s Quarters, the Master paid his respects to the Emperor, who first looked upon him.
The Buddha’s tooth relic and śarīra bestowed by Emperor Taizu of the Great Song were brought forth; the Emperor held them with his hands to his forehead in deep reverence.
The Master then presented the historical accounts of the Buddha’s tooth relic, leading [the Emperor] to the Yuyan Hall and the Xiaoxiao Pavilion.
He read a letter from Dahuì Zōnggǎo sent from Méiyáng regarding a Dharma robe, which stated: "The Layman Chāorán is one of those within [the ranks];
I fear there may be points where he has not yet reached perfection, and we should deliberate upon them together. Upon seeing this, the Emperor remarked, "It is a pity that he was two years too late;
I did not get to know Zōnggǎo. The Emperor asked, "What is Chāorán like? The Master replied, "Layman Chāorán..."
Having associated for a long time with my late teacher Yuanwu and Dahui, they instructed me to administer a severe blow to others while smiling.
Later, when I reached the front of the abbot’s quarters, I saw three volumes of recorded sayings on the desk, along with a petition for an audience.
The Emperor asked, "What is this? The Master replied, "This is what I previously requested to be presented as the *Three Patriarchs*."
The Great Master’s *Inscription on Faith* (*Xinxin Ming*), the *Biography of Tieshe’an*, and the records of previous audiences contained instructions to include these works [in the canon].
Subsequently, he arrived at the Jiaolu Chamber and saw the Master’s portrait. He then asked, "Who is this?
The Master replied, "This is the monk-disciple who painted my crown-protrusion (*uṣṇīṣa*) and requested a eulogy. The Emperor said, "This is merely a painting."
[The Emperor asked: "Which one is the true one? The Master joined his palms, bowed his body, and said: "The spring air is mild and warm;
we respectfully wish Your Majesty a myriad blessings. The Emperor laughed heartily. The Emperor looked at the portrait of Chan Master Yuanwu and read the eulogy inscribed upon it.

"What a fine, liberated old monk! He has been painted with perfect resemblance. He dwelt in the monastic centers throughout the land for eight years. Upon encountering [the portrait], he remarked: "A truly spirited old bhikṣu!"
Focusing solely on this matter, Hai-kou’s eloquence surged like a vast tide; yet, upon reaching the ultimate, he did not speak a single word.

Huiyuan seized the essential pivot of the school, bearing its burden with broad strides and long steps. In his forge, he swiftly applied tongs and hammers to uphold the path that transcends the ordinary.
The Emperor said, "This is precisely what was mentioned previously regarding Guangyao’s audience at Weiyang.
The Master replied, "It is this very image of Śākyamuni Emerging from the Mountains that Your Majesty is viewing. The Master further reported, "This is a painting by Wu Daozi."
The Master also read the eulogy he had inscribed: "How great is Śākyamuni! An ocean of merit, immeasurable.
Here, vermilion is scarce; red earth serves as the best pigment. I now prostrate and offer praise, leaving this as a model for humans and devas.
Looking up at the image of Linji, he said, "This is Linji. The Master then reported, "The Chan Master Linji was originally from Cao..."
The man from the province was the twelfth-generation patriarch. As the Emperor surveyed the mountains and forests, he remarked, "I imagine it would be wonderful to see this when the snow falls.
The Master replied, "There is something even better up above. The Emperor returned, and the Master followed him to the front of the Dharma Hall on the eastern corridor.
The Emperor observed the murals on the wall, and the Master reported, "These are the eminent monks of successive dynasties. The Emperor said, "Just as..."

The Master asked, "Is there anything now? The Emperor replied, "The work on the western corridor is already complete. The Master pointed toward the *Avataṃsaka* transformation tableau (*parivarta-vigraha*).

As the Master questioned him, the Emperor responded accordingly; their words and meanings were in perfect accord. Thereupon, the Emperor turned his carriage back. The Master expressed his gratitude and returned home.
On the following day, an imperial decree was issued granting him silk fabrics and other gifts.
The Record of the Imperial Audience for Chan Master Fohai’s Appointment to Lingyin,
Compiled by the Attendant (Subject) Monk [Name], Respectfully Submitted for Imperial Inspection.
On the sixth day of the eighth month of the eighth year of the Qiandao era, there was...

The Imperial Decree was proclaimed to the Elder of Lingyin: for seven days, officials, monks, and Daoists were to guard the gates together. [The Emperor] entered the inner quarters to partake of a vegetarian feast at the Guantang Hall.

After the meal, he proceeded to the front of the Guantang Hall to pay his respects to the Sovereign. The Sovereign granted him a seat and served tea. Following the expression of gratitude for this favor, he subsequently received...
The Imperial Decree: "I shall summon the Elder of Lingyin alone. He arrived at the East Pavilion of the Guantang Hall, and the Master followed him inside.
The Master addressed the Emperor, saying: "Today Your Majesty has bestowed upon us pure offerings. The three teachings have assembled together; such a magnificent event is rare in this world.
We are deeply moved by Your Majesty’s sacred grace. The Emperor said, "It may indeed be called a magnificent event," and granted the Master a seat. The Master immediately...
After expressing gratitude, he took his seat. The Emperor said, "I wish to ask you about one or two matters. The Master replied, "Your servant would be honored to hear Your Majesty’s instructions.
The Emperor said, "The other day, while asleep in a dream, I suddenly heard the sound of a bell and woke up.
I do not know whether the dream and the waking state are the same or different. The Master replied, "Does Your Majesty ask about that which was within the dream, or that which has come after waking?"
If you ask about that which has already awakened, this is precisely the talk of one still asleep. If you ask about that within the dream, there is no difference between dreaming and waking.
Who can be made to distinguish them? "The dream is an illusion; knowing it as an illusion is liberation from it. Being liberated from the illusion is awakening.

In the awakened mind, there is no movement. Therefore it is said: "If one can transform things, one is identical to the Tathāgata. The Emperor said: "Since dreams and illusions are not real, what then of the sound of the bell?"
“From where does it arise? The Master replied, “It arises from Your Majesty’s question.
The Emperor asked again, “The other day, while sitting in quiet meditation in this pavilion, I suddenly recalled what you previously mentioned: ‘Not being a companion to the myriad dharmas.
That very state of not being a companion to the myriad dharmas is itself extraordinary. From this point on, I have attained a certain insight. The Master replied, “Indeed.”
"He does not consort with the myriad dharmas. "Your Majesty, how do you understand this? The Emperor said, "The four seas are not too many for him.
The Master submitted, "If one were to draw up all the water of the Western River with a single mouth, what then? The Emperor said, "There has never been any deficiency.
The Master submitted, "Whenever I enter the inner chamber, I ask the monks, 'What is the brand-new phrase? As I am about to open [the question]—"
[The Master] struck him immediately. "What is the mechanism of killing and giving life? [The Master] struck him as soon as he opened his mouth. "What is the upward path?
[The Master] struck him even before he had opened his mouth. The Emperor asked, "Why is it thus? The Master replied, "As soon as one thinks, it becomes a superfluous dharma.
As soon as one falls into the realm of the aggregates (skandhas), that is the very root of birth and death. Studying Chan is like riding a waterwheel."
Do not interfere with deliberation; it is like the spark struck from flint, like a flash of lightning—this is already a state of stagnation.
Why? Because in the Dharma there are no two dharmas; in seeing there is no dualistic seeing; in the mind there is no separate mind; as there are not two suns in the sky.
Therefore, when Deshan realized the Way, he sealed the doors of the Buddha Hall and said: "When you exist, I do not; when I exist, you do not."
Only then can one see the Way. Recently, a scholar came to the temple and, seeing the verses composed by [the Subject] on the wall of the abbot’s quarters, remarked, "Excellent verses!
[The Subject] asked him, "I have heard that you study the teachings of Yi-chuan and reject those of the Buddha."
"Is this so? The scholar said, "No, it is not. (The Subject) asked again, "For instance, when Deshan addressed the assembly, he said, 'Śākyamuni and Maitreya are dung-carriers;
Bodhisattvas of the Ten Stages are field-watchers. Is this also slandering the Buddha? The scholar was bewildered.
(The Subject) said, "Right here, however, there is a living path. If you can see it, you will enjoy its benefits."
"Exhausted! It is as if one looks but does not see. Not only does this involve the cause bringing forth the fruit, but there is more to it than that.

they then give rise to interpretations following those words. The illness lies in the failure to sever the life-root (*mūla*); they seem to believe, yet do not believe; it seems as if it exists..."

The Emperor said, "How can one penetrate through this? The Master replied, "Throughout past and present, the patriarchs have each employed blows and shouts according to their own fundamental principles.

The Emperor said, "If it were not for your explanation, how could I have known this? The Master replied, "A Chan practitioner’s Chan-mechanism (*chanji*) often clarifies mechanisms that transcend the conventional.

A soldier’s military mechanism is such that while his eyes watch the southeast, his intent lies in the northwest; it is like a person playing chess—this is called the movement of mechanism (*jixing*).
The Patriarch said: 'Where the wheel of mechanism turns, even the skilled author is still deluded. Only when the thousand eyes are suddenly opened [is one enlightened]."
Meeting with you, the Chan practitioners speak of Chan: one thrust and one parry, one emergence and one submergence;

release and capture are within their own power, killing and giving life are applied according to the moment. It is as if Sun Wu employs his troops—like a pearl rolling on a tray, like a tray rolling a pearl;

After returning from Linhai, [the Master] took up residence west of Changmen; it was only three or four *li* from Huqiu. Amidst the clamor of worldly entanglements, several months passed without being able to fulfill the agreement.
One morning at dawn, [the author] went to visit him, only to find the Master already at the guest house, as if he had known in advance.
The official in charge looked at him and smiled; he detained him and engaged him in conversation.

His words were like startling thunder and flashing lightning, like a tempestuous wind and pelting rain, yet suddenly it was as if the sky were clear and the sun bright, the rivers luminous and the mountains tranquil.

Because Devadatta slandered the Buddha, the World-Honored One entered hell in his physical body. He then had Ānanda inquire on his behalf: "Are you at peace within hell?
Devadatta replied, "Though I am in hell, it is as pleasant as the third dhyāna heaven.
The Buddha again had Ānanda ask, "Do you still seek to leave? Devadatta replied, "I shall leave as soon as the World-Honored One arrives. Thus spoke Ānanda.
He said, "The Buddha is the Great Teacher of the three realms; how could he have any portion that enters hell?
Since the Buddha has no portion that enters hell, how could I have any portion that exits hell?"
